title: Systematic elimination of local gravitational models on the SPARC 175 sample: Evidence for an irreducible galaxy-specific degree of freedom
description: This paper performs a systematic elimination study of baryon-based rotation-curve models on the SPARC 175 sample. It shows that all purely local multiplicative models with only global parameters fail in low-acceleration (FLOW) galaxies, while a minimal hybrid model with a single galaxy-specific amplitude matches NFW halo fit performance with half the per-galaxy parameters. The study finds the added amplitude is a stable, intrinsic galaxy property that cannot be predicted from standard baryonic observables.

RAR_mapping.description: Empirical radial-acceleration relation used to test local multiplicative laws mapping baryonic to observed acceleration.

baryonic_decomposition.description: Baryonic rotation curve with fixed mass-to-light ratios \Upsilon_d = 0.5 and \Upsilon_b = 0.7 at 3.6 µm.

multiplicative_model.description: Generic local multiplicative class tested with various functional forms and local extensions.

screening_law.description: Power-law screening interpolation used in both global tests and in the hybrid model; k locked to 0.415 during tests.

hybrid_model.description: Minimal hybrid with one galaxy-specific amplitude A_gal and global g^{\dagger}, r_0; achieves NFW-like performance with fewer per-galaxy parameters.

gradient_scale.description: Gradient length scale used in the gradient-dependent extension of \mu to test local structural information.

key_results.main_finding: All purely local multiplicative models with only global parameters are falsified on SPARC 175 (FLOW win ≈ 27%), while a one-parameter-per-galaxy hybrid matches NFW performance (FLOW win 72.6%, median χ2/dof 2.71 vs 2.64).
datasets_used: SPARC 175 rotation curves (3391 radial points across 175 galaxies; Vobs, σV≥1 km s−1, Vgas, Vdisk, Vbul)

sealed_predictions.statement: On independent low-acceleration (FLOW-like) galaxy samples, any purely local multiplicative model with only global parameters will win in ≤35% of galaxies against NFW at |ΔAIC| > 10.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Blind application to new high-quality rotation-curve datasets (e.g., SPARC extensions or similar) with the same fitting protocol and AIC threshold.

sealed_predictions.statement: The per-galaxy amplitude A_gal will remain orthogonal to standard baryonic observables (R^2 ≤ 0.10) and retain stable sign (>70% agreement) under re-observation and radial-subset cross-validation.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Re-fitting the hybrid model on new or deeper data and testing A_gal predictability from baryonic properties plus sign stability across radial subsets.

kill_criteria: KC1: Demonstrate a zero per-galaxy local model µ(g, local info) with only global parameters that achieves FLOW win rate ≥70% and median χ2/dof comparable to or better than NFW on SPARC and an independent dataset, with shuffle tests confirming genuine use of the local variable(s).

KC2: Show that A_gal can be accurately predicted from baryonic observables (e.g., mass, size, surface density, gradients, angular velocity) with R^2 ≥ 0.5 and stable sign prediction, eliminating the need for a free per-galaxy amplitude.
KC3: Cross-validation instability: leave-one-out or radial-subset tests reduce A_gal stability to ρ < 0.2 or inflate median CV error to >50%, indicating A_gal is not an intrinsic property.

KC4: Allowing reasonable baryonic systematics (e.g., variable mass-to-light ratios within accepted ranges) removes the performance gap so that a global-parameter local model matches NFW (|ΔAIC| ≤ 10 in the majority of FLOW galaxies) without per-galaxy amplitudes.

KC5: On an independent high-quality rotation-curve sample, the hybrid model underperforms NFW decisively (|ΔAIC| > 10) in a majority of galaxies and/or exhibits unstable A_gal sign (<50% agreement), contradicting claims of robustness.

KC6: Replication shows the reported eliminations arise from numerical artefacts (e.g., smoothing, binning, noise handling), evidenced by results reversing under validated alternative pipelines or by failed shuffle controls (p < 0.01) for gradient/surface-density models.
